parameters_yaml:
# Account parameters — every assumption lives here, never hardcoded in modules.
# Values sourced from the verified lit review + DATA.md PART E5. Each carries a
# source + an uncertainty band (used by the Monte-Carlo in uncertainty/).

# ⚠️ RED-TEAM R1: utilisation & PUE are the dominant assumed scalars — the account's
# ABSOLUTE magnitude scales with them. Mitigations: (a) lead with RELATIVE/spatial
# results (a *global* scalar cancels in ranking); (b) type-specific values below;
# (c) calibrate the aggregate (account/calibrate.py). Because type-specific values do
# NOT fully cancel, rankings are sensitivity-tested against the type mix (R1 residual).
energy:
  # E_IT = capacity_MW * utilisation * hours(month); E_grid = E_IT * PUE
  utilisation:            # IT load factor (no per-facility data -> modeled, by type)
    by_facility_type:
      hyperscale: {default: 0.70, band: [0.55, 0.85]}
      colocation: {default: 0.45, band: [0.30, 0.65]}
      enterprise: {default: 0.40, band: [0.25, 0.60]}
      unknown:    {default: 0.55, band: [0.40, 0.75]}   # fallback = global mid
    source: "modeled (no per-facility utilisation dataset exists; DATA.md E4)"
  # Stated capacities that are TOTAL FACILITY power, not IT capacity. The India list tags each MW
  # figure (datasets/india_dc_facilities, Notes & Method: "mixes IT, critical-IT and total-facility
  # bases"); operational_total rows are converted with the facility PUE, C_IT = C / PUE (account/energy.py),
  # the same rule as US facility-basis records. operational_IT and operational_critical are IT load.
  facility_power_capacity_bases: [operational_total]
  pue:
    by_facility_type:
      hyperscale: {default: 1.2, band: [1.1, 1.4]}
      colocation: {default: 1.6, band: [1.4, 1.9]}
      enterprise: {default: 1.7, band: [1.5, 2.0]}
      unknown:    {default: 1.55, band: [1.2, 1.9]}
    by_operator:          # override where disclosed (fleet averages, DATA.md §D)
      microsoft: 1.17
      meta: 1.08
      aws: 1.14
      google: 1.09

water_onsite:             # scope-1 WUE (L per kWh IT), fleet-average -> wide band
  wue_default:
    default: 1.9          # industry avg (Green Grid / DATA.md E5) — also the MC triangular mode
    band: [0.7, 2.5]      # efficient (NREL 0.7) .. evaporative-cooling upper end 2.5
    # Upper bound 2.5 L/kWh (decision 2026-09-27): Equinix, "What Is Water Usage Effectiveness
    # (WUE) in Data Centers?" (blog, 2024-11-13): "0 L/kWh (with air cooling) or up to 2.5 L/kWh
    # (with evaporative cooling)"; cf. Equinix 2025 Sustainability Report p.26: fleet WUE 0.91,
    # evaporative sites 1.41. ISO/IEC 30134-9:2022 DEFINES WUE but sets no limits or targets.
    # Replaces 9 L/kWh (Li et al. 2304.03271: on-site WUE 0.01-9 across sites/seasons, not an
    # annual-average range).
  # constant = wue_default everywhere (round 5); climate = cooling-tower WUE at the facility's monthly
  # wet-bulb temperature (Gupta et al. 2024, ACM e-Energy, eq. "fixed cold water"; NASA POWER T2MWET),
  # see account/wue.py. Disclosed operator WUEs below override either.
  wue_model: climate
  wue_by_operator:
    microsoft: 0.27
    meta: 0.19
    aws: 0.12
    # google: publishes NO fleet WUE -> derive + flag (DATA.md §D)

water_grid:               # scope-2 EWIF = sum(fuel_share * macknick_coeff)
  macknick_source: "Macknick et al. 2012 ERL 7:045802 (data/macknick), recirculating consumption"
  # fuel crosswalk Ember Variable -> Macknick tech (DATA.md F1). L/MWh consumption.
  ewif_coeff_L_per_MWh:
    Coal: 2600
    Gas: 750             # NGCC recirculating
    Nuclear: 2540
    Bioenergy: 2600
    Hydro: 17000         # reservoir evaporation (huge; flag/sensitivity)
    Solar: 100           # PV
    Wind: 0
    Other Fossil: 1800   # default
    Other Renewables: 500
  note: "US coefficients applied to IN/EU -> representativeness caveat + sensitivity"
  # Hydro's 17,000 L/MWh is reservoir evaporation attributed wholly to power; run-of-river
  # and multi-purpose reservoirs argue for far less. The MC samples a multiplier on the hydro
  # coefficient over this band (0 = no evaporation attributed to power, 1 = full Macknick).
  hydro_multiplier_band: [0.0, 1.0]

# Grid zone used for carbon CI, scope-2 EWIF and scope-2 scarcity (generation basins).
# state    = Ember state-month generation mix (generation-based, NOT consumption; R2 caveat)
# national = Ember India-total month (the pooled synchronous-grid reading)
# CEA national-annual EF is kept only as a cross-check when data/cea/ is present.
grid:
  zone: state
  # India carbon basis: generation = Ember state own-generation mix (R2 caveat); consumption =
  # Electricity Maps regional flow-traced (import-adjusted) CI, which removes R2. Falls back to
  # generation if the EM key/cache is absent. US/EU unaffected (EM covers India zones only).
  carbon_basis: consumption
  account_year: 2024
  gem_path: "data/gem/Global-Integrated-Power-March-2026-II.xlsx"
  gadm_path: "data/gadm/gadm41_IND.gpkg"     # GADM 4.1, layer ADM_ADM_1, field NAME_1
  # GEM plant state of record = GADM from coordinates (io/gem.assign_state_of_record), except
  # these reviewed cases from results/gem_gadm_state_mismatches.csv (decision 2026-09-27):
  gem_state_overrides:
    G100000800551: {state: Karnataka, note: "Vijaypura (Adani) II - GEM coordinates (26.84N 77.10E) fall in Rajasthan 911 km out; sister farms I/III are in Karnataka; coordinate error, label kept, coordinate NOT corrected"}
    G100000108490: {state: Chhattisgarh, note: "Rawan Cement - GEM coordinates fall in Rajasthan 693 km out; coordinate error, label kept, coordinate NOT corrected"}
    G100000833894: {state: Gujarat, note: "Gujarat (Adani) IV Hybrid - coordinates at Khavda, Gujarat; GEM label Rajasthan treated as the error"}
  gem_state_ambiguous:
    G100000601967: "Lower Sileru hydro - GEM Andhra Pradesh | GADM Telangana (8.8 km from the AP polygon); unresolved, no single-state assignment"
  # GEM 'Type' -> Ember fuel (the Macknick coefficient key)
  gem_type_to_fuel:
    coal: Coal
    oil/gas: Gas
    nuclear: Nuclear
    hydropower: Hydro
    bioenergy: Bioenergy
    utility-scale solar: Solar
    wind: Wind
    geothermal: Other Renewables

inference:
  # ⚠️ R13: this is a SCOPING sensitivity range, NOT per-facility attribution (no dataset
  # separates inference per facility). Report the range; do not claim discrimination.
  sectoral_share:
    default: 0.85
    band: [0.80, 0.90]
    source: "LBNL/IEA ~80-90% operational (DATA.md §G)"

scarcity:
  method: "AWARE2.0 native monthly basin CF (data/aware gpkg); SEPARATE column, never blended"
  # ⚠️ R3: scarcity-weighting is RIGOROUS only for scope-1 (on-site water, at the DC's own
  # basin). Scope-2 (grid) water is consumed at the POWER PLANTS (pooled grid, other basins)
  # -> it is NOT basin-localisable; weight scope-2 at the grid-region average, flagged coarse.
  # => the defensible scarcity story leads with SCOPE-1; scope-2 scarcity is a bounded add-on.
  scope1_weighting: basin_of_facility        # rigorous
  scope2_weighting: grid_region_average      # coarse, flagged
  # ⚠️ R9: AWARE CF=100 is the CAP (max scarcity / arid-undefined), not a plain value.
  cap: 100
  cap_semantics: "100 = capped max scarcity; io/aware.py flags capped & no-data basins"
  drought_caveat: "AWARE = 12-month CLIMATOLOGY (no year) -> misses drought-year events (R10)"

# ⚠️ R12: define the finding metric explicitly (rankings differ by metric).
outputs:
  primary_metric: scarcity_weighted_m3_per_year   # + cumulative-to-2030 (with L3)
  secondary_metrics: [physical_m3_per_year, tco2_per_year, scarcity_weighted_m3_per_MW]
  lead_result: spatial_distribution               # ROBUST CORE: basin burden ranking
  absolutes_reported_as: calibrated_range         # never point estimates (R1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COUNTERFACTUAL LEVERS (L3 / G6) — each = a parameter transform on the account.
# Values from engineering/industry lit (DATA.md E5). Verify exact values at build.
levers:
  mandatory_disclosure:
    type: coverage
    effect: "raises measured-coverage; models the *revealed* footprint vs current opacity"
  coastal_seawater_siting:
    type: wue_override
    new_wue: 0.1          # seawater/WSAC: near-zero freshwater (periodic salt flush)
    applies_to: "new/relocatable load in coastal zones"
  zero_liquid_discharge:
    # ZLD treats and reuses cooling-tower BLOWDOWN; it does not touch evaporation. Tower mass balance:
    # make-up M = E + B with blowdown B = E / (N - 1) at N cycles of concentration (drift neglected), so
    # B / M = 1 / N, and ZLD saves recovery x (1/N) of make-up (on-site) water:
    #   saving_fraction = blowdown_recovery / cycles_of_concentration  (= 0.92 / 5 = 18.4%)
    # Round 5 applied 0.92 to ALL on-site water, which treated evaporation as recoverable (about 5x too high).
    # On-site water (WUE) is read as site make-up water (ISO/IEC 30134-9 water INPUT). Under a strictly
    # consumptive reading the discharged blowdown is returned water, so ZLD saves ~0 consumption: the
    # saving below is an upper bound. Sources: US DOE FEMP, "Cooling Towers: Understanding Key Components of
    # Cooling Towers and How to Improve Water Efficiency" (2011), cycles 3-7 typical, B = E/(N-1);
    # recovery ~0.90-0.95 of blowdown for thermal/membrane ZLD trains.
    type: recycle
    cycles_of_concentration: 5
    cycles_band: [3, 7]
    blowdown_recovery: 0.92
    blowdown_recovery_band: [0.90, 0.95]
    applies_to: scope1        # on-site cooling water only; power-plant (scope-2) water is untouched
  efficiency_standard:
    type: pue_wue_cap
    pue_cap: 1.3
    wue_cap: 0.7          # NREL-efficient
    tradeoff: "liquid/mechanical cooling: water down BUT PUE/energy/carbon up -> model both"

regions:
  tiering: {India: deep, US: solid, EU: light}
  # ⚠️ R2: a DC consumes the POOLED regional/national grid, not its state's generation mix.
  # -> carbon must be CONSUMPTION-based at the grid region, NOT state generation-CI.
  carbon_working_source:
    India: ember_state_monthly        # set by grid.zone; generation-based -> R2 caveat stated in results
    India_pooled_alternative: ember_national_monthly   # grid.zone: national
    India_crosscheck: cea_national_annual              # only if data/cea/ is present
    US: egrid_eia_subregion_monthly   # region_config.US.grid_source: eia_egrid (io/us_grid.py); ember_macknick = round-5 sensitivity
    EU: ember_country_monthly         # no sub-national -> light tier
  # => India sub-national NOVELTY rides on WATER (local), not carbon (regional). Stated.
  comparison_unit: per_MW_and_basin_level   # ⚠️ R11: common normalised unit for the cross-region gradient

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Q3 ROUTING (L6) — stylised monthly environment.
routing:
  solver: price_decomposition   # price_decomposition (agents, routing/agents.py) | central_lp (verification)
  flexible_share: 0.3       # fraction of load that can move between facilities
  max_util: 0.90            # a facility can run up to this utilisation
  V: 1.0                    # drift-plus-penalty weight (swept in v_sweep)
  v_sweep: [0.1, 1.0, 10.0]
  lambda: 1.0               # scarcity water vs carbon weight (both normalised to mean 1)
  demand_noise: 0.05
  seeds: 10
  # Basin water budget R_hat_b(m), DECOUPLED from datacenter use and taken from AWARE 2.0
  # (Seitfudem et al. 2025, doi:10.5281/zenodo.15133241):
  #   R_hat_b(m) = alpha * max(AMD_b(m), 0) * area_b
  # AMD = water available minus human consumption minus environmental water requirements
  # (EWR), per area and month. alpha = 1 is the parameter-free headline: datacenters may not
  # draw more than the water left after people and environmental flows; any draw in a month
  # with AMD <= 0 is an overdraft. Smaller alpha = a smaller sector share (budget_sweep).
  # Basin queues track SCOPE-1 water only (scope-2 is drawn at power-plant basins).
  budget_alpha: 1.0
  budget_sweep_alpha: [1.0, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001]
  aware_intermediate_path: "data/aware/AWARE20_Intermediate_Variables.xlsx"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Q1 SITING (L7).
siting:
  new_facility_mw: 50       # size S of the hypothetical new facility
  new_facility_type: colocation
  weight_samples: 500
  small_grid_twh: 10        # states generating < this (TWh/yr) are flagged: their own-generation CI is not what a DC would draw
  # candidate cells = (state x AWARE basin) cells holding >=1 operating GEM plant,
  # plus every cell that already holds a datacenter
  # 2030/2050 scenarios: Aqueduct 4.0 0-5 water-stress scores (baseline bws_score vs future ws_x_s,
  # bau/opt/pes x 2030/2050) as a fifth criterion; minimax regret over weights x scenarios.
  # Scores not raw ratios: raw ws is capped at 1 and futures are bias-corrected to baseline (Kuzma et al. 2023 pp.10-11)
  aqueduct_gdb_path: "data/aqueduct/Aq40_Y2023D07M05.gdb"
  # 2030/2050 carbon (project/carbon_future.py): each zone's account-year CI x (official path in the
  # scenario year / path in the account year). One central path per region, paired with every water
  # pathway of that year. Fixed before the run (2026-10-14); see docs/data_sources.md.
  carbon_future:
    India:      # national only: same factor for every state
      kind: national_path
      source: "CEA National Electricity Plan 2022-32 Vol I (Generation), notified May 2023: average CO2 emission factor 0.548 (FY 2026-27) and 0.430 (FY 2031-32) kg CO2/kWh net"
      points: {2026: 0.548, 2031: 0.430}    # keyed by FY start year (FY 2026-27 -> 2026)
      base: cea_database                    # account-year value = CEA CO2 Baseline Database V22, FY starting in the account year
      after_last: hold                      # no official path beyond FY 2031-32: held (stated in the report)
    US:
      kind: cambium_lrmer_states
      path: "data/carbon_future/Cambium22_LRMER_states.xlsx"   # NREL Cambium 2022 LRMER workbook, states (Gagnon et al. 2023)
      scenario: Mid-case
      metric: "CO2 from Direct Combustion"  # direct, like Ember's CI
    EU:
      kind: eu_ref2020
      path: "data/carbon_future/ref2020_energy-transport-ghg.xlsx"  # EU Reference Scenario 2020, country sheets
      row_label: "Electricity and Steam production (tCO2/MWh)"     # carbon intensity indicator, <CC>_B sheets

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# L8 UNCERTAINTY
uncertainty:
  # triangular = mode at the point estimate, support = the sourced band (a best estimate exists)
  # uniform    = every value in the band equally likely (reported alongside as a sensitivity)
  # WUE band is [0.7, 2.5] with mode 1.9 (see water_onsite.wue_default for sources).
  distribution: triangular
  n_samples: 4000
  # Saltelli design for the account Sobol indices: sobol_n_samples x (k + 2) analytic evaluations
  # (cheap); 2^15 keeps the bootstrap 90% interval on each first-order index within about +-0.05.
  sobol_n_samples: 32768
  # Routing Monte Carlo (uncertainty/routing_mc.py): the Q3 comparison re-run per draw, so the
  # carbon/water trade-off gets an interval instead of a point. Each draw also takes its own
  # demand-noise seed. ci_zone_band is a per-zone multiplier on grid CI, drawn independently per
  # zone (ASSUMPTION, not sourced: +-10% relative uncertainty between grid zones, which is what
  # moves routing carbon); set [1.0, 1.0] to switch it off.
  routing_n_samples: 1000
  ci_zone_band: [0.9, 1.1]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# REGIONS (L0/L1 inputs per region; the India block mirrors grid.* above)
region_config:
  India:
    tier: facility
    account_year: 2024
    gem_countries: [India]
    gadm_path: "data/gadm/gadm41_IND.gpkg"
  US:
    tier: facility
    account_year: 2024
    gem_countries: [United States]
    gadm_path: "data/gadm/gadm41_USA.gpkg"
    compute_atlas_path: "data/compute_atlas/facilities_v1.34.0.json"   # pinned release v1.34.0 (CC BY 4.0)
    # US grid carbon + power-plant water source (io/us_grid.py):
    #   eia_egrid       zone = eGRID subregion; carbon = EIA-923 monthly plant generation x eGRID plant
    #                   CO2 rates; water = EIA reported cooling-water consumption per plant (Macknick
    #                   only for plants that do not report); scarcity at each plant's own basin.
    #   ember_macknick  zone = state; Ember state generation mix x Macknick fuel coefficients (round 5).
    grid_source: eia_egrid
    egrid_year: 2023                    # latest eGRID (rev2, June 2025); plant rates applied to 2024 generation
    egrid_path: "data/egrid/egrid2023_data_rev2.xlsx"
    egrid_subregions_path: "data/egrid/subregions/eGRID2023_Subregions.shp"
    eia923_path: "data/eia/f923_{year}/EIA923_Schedules_2_3_4_5_M_12_{year}_Final*.xlsx"
    eia_cooling_path: "data/eia/Cooling_Boiler_Generator_Data_Summary_{year}.xlsx"
    eia860_plant_path: "data/eia/eia860_2024/2___Plant_Y2024.xlsx"     # locations of plants not in eGRID
  EU:
    tier: country            # facility data confidential under Reg (EU) 2024/1364
    account_year: 2023       # first EED reporting period covers calendar 2023
    gem_countries: [Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland,
                    France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta,
                    Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden]
    eu_eed_path: "dcfootprint/config/eu_member_state_2023.csv"   # rebuilt by experiments/extract_eu_tables.py
    aware_country_path: "data/aware/AWARE20_Countries_and_Regions.xlsx"
    aware_country_sheet: CFs_nonagri     # non-agricultural use = industrial/datacenter water
